about.label: About
about.title: Who am I?
about.intro: I'm Marc Antoine. I design and build complete web applications, from the database all the way to the interface.
about.body: I love turning a fuzzy idea into a concrete product that is fast and pleasant to use — on phones and desktops alike. I mostly build with Next.js, React and TypeScript, with Node.js and MongoDB on the server, and ship everything with Docker.
about.body2: I build web platforms for clients through an agency, like bilingual online contests. And when I'm not coding for a client, I build my own self-hosted tools: a camera to keep an eye on my cats, a media library manager… and this portfolio.

concours.name: Contest Platform
concours.tagline: A white-label platform for running bilingual online contests, from entry form to prize draw.
concours.description: Concours lets a marketing team launch branded contests on their own domains without a developer: a 7-step wizard covers settings, entry form questions, design, rules, emails, prize waivers and domain. Participants enter through a mobile-first public site with address autocomplete and a confirmation code. Staff manage entries, draws, winners and prize shipping from a role-based back office.

features.title: No-code contest wizard
features.text: Admins build the entry form with drag-and-drop questions, upload backgrounds per screen size with a form safe zone, and edit FR/EN rules in a rich-text editor.

features.title: Draws and winner tracking
features.text: A random prize draw respects stock per prize and per branch, then each winner goes through statuses from waiver sent to prize shipped.

features.title: Contest variants
features.text: Besides standard contests, it handles grouped contests split across store branches (with a nearest-branch lookup) and purchase incentives with proof of purchase and reward approval.

features.title: Secure back office
features.text: Custom roles with per-section permissions, two-factor login, trusted devices, an audit log and Excel exports of participations.

concours.architecture: Turborepo + pnpm monorepo with four apps (Next.js admin, Next.js public contest site, a node-cron worker and an email-queue worker) sharing a package of Mongoose models, services, Zod schemas and React components. MongoDB stores everything; emails are queued in the database and sent by the worker through Microsoft Graph, and the cron worker expires prize waivers, sends reminders and syncs custom domains to Caddy, which handles TLS automatically. Both sites are bilingual with next-intl (fr-CA/en-CA, localized URLs) and ship as Docker images via Docker Compose.

molson.name: Your team. Your Molson.
molson.tagline: Bilingual hockey-team contest for Molson, exclusive to Couche-Tard in Québec.
molson.description: A mobile-first promotional contest where adults in Québec form hockey teams of up to 11 players. Each player picks a jersey name, number and position, then earns points through daily check-ins and Molson purchases backed by a receipt. Every point counts as an entry in a weighted draw for personalized team uniforms. A full admin back office lets the brand moderate entries and run the draw.

features.title: Team building
features.text: Captains create a team with a name and color, then invite teammates by email or share link, up to 11 players.

features.title: Points & receipts
features.text: Players claim daily points and submit Molson purchases with a compressed receipt photo, limited to one product entry per day.

features.title: Passwordless sign-in
features.text: Sign-up with an age gate and Altcha captcha, then one-time codes sent by email, JWT sessions and CSRF protection.

features.title: Admin & draw
features.text: Filterable tables of teams, users and points with receipt review, disqualification, and a draw where each team's odds match its share of total points.

molson.architecture: Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript, HeroUI and Tailwind. API route handlers sit on a services/repositories layer over MongoDB (Mongoose, replica-set transactions). Locale comes from the domain via next-intl (French and English subdomains with translated paths). A separate node-cron worker calls token-protected endpoints for weekly score emails (React Email + Resend) and cleanup, and opted-in users sync to Cyberimpact.

catcam.name: La Catcam
catcam.meta: Self-hosted · Front end for Shinobi NVR
catcam.tagline: A warm, mobile-first window on the cats at home, built on top of a Shinobi NVR.
catcam.description: Catcam is a self-hosted web app for checking on the house cats from anywhere. It sits in front of a Shinobi network video recorder: you sign in with your Shinobi account, then watch any camera live or browse motion recordings by thumbnail, from a phone or a desktop browser.

features.title: Live camera feeds
features.text: HLS livestreams played with hls.js, with a one-tap camera switcher and an HQ/SQ quality toggle.

features.title: Recordings browser
features.text: A thumbnail grid of recent clips with infinite scroll, per-camera filtering and time-range presets or a custom date-time picker.

features.title: Custom video player
features.text: Overlay controls, seek bar, previous/next clip, fullscreen and double-tap to skip back or forward on mobile.

features.title: Per-user preferences
features.text: Light, dark or automatic (time-of-day) theme, default camera, home page and stream quality, plus admin switches to turn cameras on or off.

catcam.architecture: Next.js 16 (App Router, React 19, TypeScript) with Tailwind CSS 4. Next.js route handlers act as a proxy to the Shinobi API for logins, monitors, videos, HLS manifests and segments, and thumbnails, which are resized on the fly with sharp, so the Shinobi server is never exposed to the browser. Sessions are signed JWT cookies (jose) checked in the Next.js proxy, and settings are saved as one JSON file per user. The app ships as a standalone Docker image that GitHub Actions builds and pushes to GHCR.

jelly.name: Jelly
jelly.tagline: A self-hosted companion for Jellyfin that takes media from search to a tidy library.
jelly.description: Jelly is a self-hosted media library and download manager built for a home Jellyfin server. It searches multiple indexers through Jackett, sends downloads to qBittorrent and tracks their progress, then parses finished files to rename and move them into the right movie or show library, with live transfer progress streamed over WebSockets.

features.title: Smart file sorting
features.text: Parses titles, years, seasons and episodes from file names, matches existing show folders, and lets you fix, ignore or bulk-edit files before moving them.

features.title: Live transfer progress
features.text: A dedicated file server copies files to their libraries and streams per-file and overall progress to every open browser through a WebSocket relay.

features.title: Multi-indexer search
features.text: Queries Jackett's Torznab API across all configured indexers or a single one, with category filters and sorting by date, seeds, size or name.

features.title: Episode trackers
features.text: Remembers the shows you follow, checks the library for the last episode on disk and searches for the next one in one click.

jelly.architecture: A Next.js 16 (App Router, React 19) app runs alongside a WebSocket relay server and an Express file server, orchestrated in development by Turborepo and bundled with tsup for production. Docker Compose deploys the three processes next to Jackett, qBittorrent and FlareSolverr, which run behind a Gluetun WireGuard VPN container. A first-run setup screen creates a single account (bcrypt-hashed password), sessions use a signed JWT cookie checked by a Next.js proxy, and UI preferences are kept per browser in a cookie.
